#!/bin/sh
# Terminal-Bench install script for the fa coding agent.
# Runs inside the task container as the tmux user (root).
set -e

mkdir -p /opt/fa
tar -xzf /installed-agent/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/fa
chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah
ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa

# Pre-seed a system-level git identity so git-touching tasks don't burn
# agent turns on `Author identity unknown` (gh-1210). System scope keeps
# repo-local config winning, so tasks whose subject is broken git config
# keep their premise. The trailing || true turns every failure path of the
# list — git-less image, failed write — into a no-op: set -e exempts the
# non-final commands of an && list but NOT the final one, so the bare list
# would still abort the install on a failed user.email write.
command -v git >/dev/null &&
    git config --system user.name fa-bench &&
    git config --system user.email fa@bench.local || true

# No user is present during benchmark runs; autopilot skips the
# critical-pattern bash interceptor that headless mode would deny.
mkdir -p ~/.fah
grep -q approvalMode ~/.fah/config.yaml 2>/dev/null ||
    printf 'approvalMode: autopilot\n' > ~/.fah/config.yaml

fa --version

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Accuracy summary for terminal-bench run dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]

Reads every <runs-dir>/*/results.json (sharded runs pin --run-id, so one
subdir per shard) and prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown accuracy table,
also appending it to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

Token/cost columns (issue #1123): total_input/output_tokens come from the
trial's fa session records (folded in by fa_agent.py at perform_task time).
Per-trial cost is derived from the pinned price table bench/pricing.json
($/Mtok, data not code); the model id is taken from the trial's synced
session records when present, else --model (or the MODEL /
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env), else the cost renders n/a — never a made-up
price. Tokens estimated where a provider omitted usage (chars/4, done by
fa_agent.py) are flagged in a note when > 0.

Issue #1339: rows whose recorded totals were lost (tb's flat-cap timeout
fabrication discards the adapter's fold — gh-1209) re-fold their usage
from the synced session logs; an agent_timeout trial that did real work
after a zero-byte takeover classifies as `recovered`, distinct from
provider hang and cap exhaustion; a test_timeout trial reads as a
terminal `no (test_timeout)` in the resolved column, while other
unresolved modes render honest `pending (mode)`; and the
unpriced line names the model ids it could not price (or says the id is
unknown).

tb exits 0 even with unresolved tasks, so the exit code is the verdict on
run COMPLETENESS only. Issue #1392 AC6: a lost/cancelled shard degrades
to an explicit `coverage: X/N` note (green-with-note) — the red verdict
is reserved for real defects: nothing produced at all, or the AC8
score-honesty contradiction (an `agent_timeout` trial whose session
shows steady sub-threshold inter-record gaps, i.e. the round-2 "killed
mid-work" class the progress-aware ladder was built to retire).
--no-fail turns the verdict off (informational per-shard tallies).

Issue #1392 AC2: the report also carries request-latency p50/p95 per
concurrency level (from each trial's bench_metrics.json) and tags the
run's concurrency level (BENCH_CONCURRENCY env, set by bench.yml's
max-concurrent input).
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

def _parse_args(argv):
    """Parse [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID].

    Single parse point (the reviewer's thread 6): --model without a
    non-empty value is a loud usage error, never a silent env fallback;
    a non-numeric expected-count is the same. Falls back to the MODEL /
    FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env only when no --model was given.
    """
    no_fail = False
    model = None
    positional = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--no-fail":
            no_fail = True
        elif arg == "--model":
            if i + 1 >= len(argv) or not argv[i + 1]:
                print(
                    "[summary] error: --model requires a model id", file=sys.stderr
                )
                sys.exit(2)
            model = argv[i + 1]
            i += 1
        else:
            positional.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if not positional:
        print(
            "[summary] error: usage: summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir>"
            " [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    try:
        expected = int(positional[1]) if len(positional) > 1 else None
    except ValueError:
        print(
            f"[summary] error: expected-count must be an integer, got:"
            f" {positional[1]!r}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    if model is None:
        model = os.environ.get("MODEL")
    if model is None:
        config = os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG")
        if config:
            try:
                model = json.loads(config).get("model")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                print(
                    "[summary] warning: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is not JSON — "
                    "ignoring it for the model id",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
    return no_fail, Path(positional[0]), expected, model


def _session_facts(runs_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """trial_name → {"model": str|None, "estimated": int,
    "input_tokens": int, "output_tokens": int} from synced sessions.

    tb ships each trial's fa sessions in the run artifacts. The glob is
    pinned to the two shipped layouts — <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent-logs/
    fah-sessions (tb sync) and <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent/fah-sessions
    (older artifact shape) — and warns loudly when a run with results has
    no session logs at all, so a layout drift can't silently zero the
    cost columns. Best-effort overall: old artifacts just yield no facts.
    """
    facts = {}
    try:
        candidates = list(runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent-logs/fah-sessions")) + list(
            runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent/fah-sessions")
        )
    except OSError:
        candidates = []
    if not candidates:
        # Only reachable when at least one results.json exists, so this is
        # a real run whose session logs went missing or drifted layout.
        print(
            f"[summary] warning: no fa session logs found "
            f"(*/*/*/agent*/fah-sessions under {runs_dir}) — per-trial model "
            f"unknown, cost renders n/a unless --model/env provides one",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    for sessions in candidates:
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(sessions)
        models = sorted(m for m in usage.models if m)
        facts[sessions.parent.parent.name] = {
            # One model per trial is the norm; mixed → None (cost n/a).
            "model": models[0] if len(models) == 1 else None,
            "estimated": usage.estimated_tokens,
            # Issue #1339: the fold fa_agent.py writes into results.json
            # can be discarded by tb's flat-cap timeout fabrication, so
            # keep the session-side totals for the summary's re-fold.
            "input_tokens": usage.input_tokens + usage.estimated_input_tokens,
            "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens + usage.estimated_output_tokens,
        }
    return facts

```yaml
      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must burn one setup minute, not 8 shards x hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the key value is never echoed (the
      # ::add-mask line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py
      # uses). Unknown provider values fail hard — never a silent
      # fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="zai glm ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi needs its capability fields declared —
              # the env preconfig carries them into the booted model
              # (catalog spec defaults would match today, an explicit
              # declaration cannot silently truncate on a catalog drift).
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":2000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash' or 'kimi-for-coding'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key base64-encoded; GitHub auto-masks
          # only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

#!/bin/sh
# Terminal-Bench install script for the fa coding agent.
# Runs inside the task container as the tmux user (root).
set -e

mkdir -p /opt/fa
tar -xzf /installed-agent/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/fa
chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah
ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa

# Pre-seed a system-level git identity so git-touching tasks don't burn
# agent turns on `Author identity unknown` (gh-1210). System scope keeps
# repo-local config winning, so tasks whose subject is broken git config
# keep their premise. The trailing || true turns every failure path of the
# list — git-less image, failed write — into a no-op: set -e exempts the
# non-final commands of an && list but NOT the final one, so the bare list
# would still abort the install on a failed user.email write.
command -v git >/dev/null &&
    git config --system user.name fa-bench &&
    git config --system user.email fa@bench.local || true

# No user is present during benchmark runs; autopilot skips the
# critical-pattern bash interceptor that headless mode would deny.
mkdir -p ~/.fah
grep -q approvalMode ~/.fah/config.yaml 2>/dev/null ||
    printf 'approvalMode: autopilot\n' > ~/.fah/config.yaml

fa --version

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Accuracy summary for terminal-bench run dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]

Reads every <runs-dir>/*/results.json (sharded runs pin --run-id, so one
subdir per shard) and prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown accuracy table,
also appending it to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

Token/cost columns (issue #1123): total_input/output_tokens come from the
trial's fa session records (folded in by fa_agent.py at perform_task time).
Per-trial cost is derived from the pinned price table bench/pricing.json
($/Mtok, data not code); the model id is taken from the trial's synced
session records when present, else --model (or the MODEL /
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env), else the cost renders n/a — never a made-up
price. Tokens estimated where a provider omitted usage (chars/4, done by
fa_agent.py) are flagged in a note when > 0.

Issue #1339: rows whose recorded totals were lost (tb's flat-cap timeout
fabrication discards the adapter's fold — gh-1209) re-fold their usage
from the synced session logs; an agent_timeout trial that did real work
after a zero-byte takeover classifies as `recovered`, distinct from
provider hang and cap exhaustion; a test_timeout trial reads as a
terminal `no (test_timeout)` in the resolved column, while other
unresolved modes render honest `pending (mode)`; and the
unpriced line names the model ids it could not price (or says the id is
unknown).

tb exits 0 even with unresolved tasks, so the exit code is the verdict on
run COMPLETENESS only. Issue #1392 AC6: a lost/cancelled shard degrades
to an explicit `coverage: X/N` note (green-with-note) — the red verdict
is reserved for real defects: nothing produced at all, or the AC8
score-honesty contradiction (an `agent_timeout` trial whose session
shows steady sub-threshold inter-record gaps, i.e. the round-2 "killed
mid-work" class the progress-aware ladder was built to retire).
--no-fail turns the verdict off (informational per-shard tallies).

Issue #1392 AC2: the report also carries request-latency p50/p95 per
concurrency level (from each trial's bench_metrics.json) and tags the
run's concurrency level (BENCH_CONCURRENCY env, set by bench.yml's
max-concurrent input).
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import bench_metrics
import fa_usage

_PRICING_PATH = Path(_BENCH_DIR) / "pricing.json"


class Row(NamedTuple):
    """One summary row.

    rec_in/rec_out: totals as recorded in results.json (0/None when tb's
    flat-cap fabrication discarded the adapter's fold). tin/tout:
    effective totals — recorded, else re-folded from the synced session
    logs (issue #1339 AC1). checklist: the gh-1412 task-ledger coverage
    cell ("checklist: V/T [ (N unmet)]" from the trial's last hidden
    `task_ledger` record, "checklist: none" when the session carries no
    ledger).
    """

    task: str
    trial: str
    mark: str
    mode: str
    rec_in: object
    rec_out: object
    tin: object
    tout: object
    cost: object
    checklist: str = "checklist: none"


def _parse_args(argv):
    """Parse [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID].

    Single parse point (the reviewer's thread 6): --model without a
    non-empty value is a loud usage error, never a silent env fallback;
    a non-numeric expected-count is the same. Falls back to the MODEL /
    FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env only when no --model was given.
    """
    no_fail = False
    model = None
    positional = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--no-fail":
            no_fail = True
        elif arg == "--model":
            if i + 1 >= len(argv) or not argv[i + 1]:
                print(
                    "[summary] error: --model requires a model id", file=sys.stderr
                )
                sys.exit(2)
            model = argv[i + 1]
            i += 1
        else:
            positional.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if not positional:
        print(
            "[summary] error: usage: summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir>"
            " [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    try:
        expected = int(positional[1]) if len(positional) > 1 else None
    except ValueError:
        print(
            f"[summary] error: expected-count must be an integer, got:"
            f" {positional[1]!r}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    if model is None:
        model = os.environ.get("MODEL")
    if model is None:
        config = os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG")
        if config:
            try:
                model = json.loads(config).get("model")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                print(
                    "[summary] warning: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is not JSON — "
                    "ignoring it for the model id",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
    return no_fail, Path(positional[0]), expected, model


def _session_facts(runs_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """trial_name → {"model": str|None, "estimated": int,
    "input_tokens": int, "output_tokens": int} from synced sessions.

    tb ships each trial's fa sessions in the run artifacts. The glob is
    pinned to the two shipped layouts — <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent-logs/
    fah-sessions (tb sync) and <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent/fah-sessions
    (older artifact shape) — and warns loudly when a run with results has
    no session logs at all, so a layout drift can't silently zero the
    cost columns. Best-effort overall: old artifacts just yield no facts.
    """
    facts = {}
    try:
        candidates = list(runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent-logs/fah-sessions")) + list(
            runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent/fah-sessions")
        )
    except OSError:
        candidates = []
    if not candidates:
        # Only reachable when at least one results.json exists, so this is
        # a real run whose session logs went missing or drifted layout.
        print(
            f"[summary] warning: no fa session logs found "
            f"(*/*/*/agent*/fah-sessions under {runs_dir}) — per-trial model "
            f"unknown, cost renders n/a unless --model/env provides one",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    for sessions in candidates:
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(sessions)
        models = sorted(m for m in usage.models if m)
        facts[sessions.parent.parent.name] = {
            # One model per trial is the norm; mixed → None (cost n/a).
            "model": models[0] if len(models) == 1 else None,
            "estimated": usage.estimated_tokens,
            # Issue #1339: the fold fa_agent.py writes into results.json
            # can be discarded by tb's flat-cap timeout fabrication, so
            # keep the session-side totals for the summary's re-fold.
            "input_tokens": usage.input_tokens + usage.estimated_input_tokens,
            "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens + usage.estimated_output_tokens,
        }
    return facts

```yaml
      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must burn one setup minute, not 8 shards x hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the key value is never echoed (the
      # ::add-mask line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py
      # uses). Unknown provider values fail hard — never a silent
      # fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="zai glm ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi needs its capability fields declared —
              # the env preconfig carries them into the booted model
              # (catalog spec defaults would match today, an explicit
              # declaration cannot silently truncate on a catalog drift).
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":2000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash' or 'kimi-for-coding'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key base64-encoded; GitHub auto-masks
          # only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

SWAP 146.=148:
+    outputs:
+      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
+      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
+      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}

+
+      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
+      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
+      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
+      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
+      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
+      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
+      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
+      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
+      - name: Resolve provider
+        id: provider
+        env:
+          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
+          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
+          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
+          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          case "$PROVIDER" in
+            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
+              provider_type=zai
+              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
+              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
+              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
+              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
+              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
+              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
+              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
+              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
+                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
+              run_label="zai glm ($model)"
+              ;;
+            kimi-for-coding)
+              provider_type=kimi
+              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
+              model='k3-256k'
+              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
+              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
+              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
+              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
+              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
+              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
+              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
+                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
+              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
+              ;;
+            *)
+              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash' or 'kimi-for-coding'"; exit 1 ;;
+          esac
+          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
+            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
+          fi
+          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
+          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
+          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
+          {
+            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
+            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
+            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
+            echo "bench_model=$model"
+            echo "run_label=$run_label"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

#!/bin/sh
# Terminal-Bench install script for the fa coding agent.
# Runs inside the task container as the tmux user (root).
set -e

mkdir -p /opt/fa
tar -xzf /installed-agent/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/fa
chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah
ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa

# Pre-seed a system-level git identity so git-touching tasks don't burn
# agent turns on `Author identity unknown` (gh-1210). System scope keeps
# repo-local config winning, so tasks whose subject is broken git config
# keep their premise. The trailing || true turns every failure path of the
# list — git-less image, failed write — into a no-op: set -e exempts the
# non-final commands of an && list but NOT the final one, so the bare list
# would still abort the install on a failed user.email write.
command -v git >/dev/null &&
    git config --system user.name fa-bench &&
    git config --system user.email fa@bench.local || true

# No user is present during benchmark runs; autopilot skips the
# critical-pattern bash interceptor that headless mode would deny.
mkdir -p ~/.fah
grep -q approvalMode ~/.fah/config.yaml 2>/dev/null ||
    printf 'approvalMode: autopilot\n' > ~/.fah/config.yaml

fa --version

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Accuracy summary for terminal-bench run dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]

Reads every <runs-dir>/*/results.json (sharded runs pin --run-id, so one
subdir per shard) and prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown accuracy table,
also appending it to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

Token/cost columns (issue #1123): total_input/output_tokens come from the
trial's fa session records (folded in by fa_agent.py at perform_task time).
Per-trial cost is derived from the pinned price table bench/pricing.json
($/Mtok, data not code); the model id is taken from the trial's synced
session records when present, else --model (or the MODEL /
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env), else the cost renders n/a — never a made-up
price. Tokens estimated where a provider omitted usage (chars/4, done by
fa_agent.py) are flagged in a note when > 0.

Issue #1339: rows whose recorded totals were lost (tb's flat-cap timeout
fabrication discards the adapter's fold — gh-1209) re-fold their usage
from the synced session logs; an agent_timeout trial that did real work
after a zero-byte takeover classifies as `recovered`, distinct from
provider hang and cap exhaustion; a test_timeout trial reads as a
terminal `no (test_timeout)` in the resolved column, while other
unresolved modes render honest `pending (mode)`; and the
unpriced line names the model ids it could not price (or says the id is
unknown).

tb exits 0 even with unresolved tasks, so the exit code is the verdict on
run COMPLETENESS only. Issue #1392 AC6: a lost/cancelled shard degrades
to an explicit `coverage: X/N` note (green-with-note) — the red verdict
is reserved for real defects: nothing produced at all, or the AC8
score-honesty contradiction (an `agent_timeout` trial whose session
shows steady sub-threshold inter-record gaps, i.e. the round-2 "killed
mid-work" class the progress-aware ladder was built to retire).
--no-fail turns the verdict off (informational per-shard tallies).

Issue #1392 AC2: the report also carries request-latency p50/p95 per
concurrency level (from each trial's bench_metrics.json) and tags the
run's concurrency level (BENCH_CONCURRENCY env, set by bench.yml's
max-concurrent input).
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import bench_metrics
import fa_usage

_PRICING_PATH = Path(_BENCH_DIR) / "pricing.json"


class Row(NamedTuple):
    """One summary row.

    rec_in/rec_out: totals as recorded in results.json (0/None when tb's
    flat-cap fabrication discarded the adapter's fold). tin/tout:
    effective totals — recorded, else re-folded from the synced session
    logs (issue #1339 AC1). checklist: the gh-1412 task-ledger coverage
    cell ("checklist: V/T [ (N unmet)]" from the trial's last hidden
    `task_ledger` record, "checklist: none" when the session carries no
    ledger).
    """

    task: str
    trial: str
    mark: str
    mode: str
    rec_in: object
    rec_out: object
    tin: object
    tout: object
    cost: object
    checklist: str = "checklist: none"


def _parse_args(argv):
    """Parse [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID].

    Single parse point (the reviewer's thread 6): --model without a
    non-empty value is a loud usage error, never a silent env fallback;
    a non-numeric expected-count is the same. Falls back to the MODEL /
    FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env only when no --model was given.
    """
    no_fail = False
    model = None
    positional = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--no-fail":
            no_fail = True
        elif arg == "--model":
            if i + 1 >= len(argv) or not argv[i + 1]:
                print(
                    "[summary] error: --model requires a model id", file=sys.stderr
                )
                sys.exit(2)
            model = argv[i + 1]
            i += 1
        else:
            positional.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if not positional:
        print(
            "[summary] error: usage: summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir>"
            " [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    try:
        expected = int(positional[1]) if len(positional) > 1 else None
    except ValueError:
        print(
            f"[summary] error: expected-count must be an integer, got:"
            f" {positional[1]!r}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    if model is None:
        model = os.environ.get("MODEL")
    if model is None:
        config = os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG")
        if config:
            try:
                model = json.loads(config).get("model")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                print(
                    "[summary] warning: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is not JSON — "
                    "ignoring it for the model id",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
    return no_fail, Path(positional[0]), expected, model


def _session_facts(runs_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """trial_name → {"model": str|None, "estimated": int,
    "input_tokens": int, "output_tokens": int} from synced sessions.

    tb ships each trial's fa sessions in the run artifacts. The glob is
    pinned to the two shipped layouts — <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent-logs/
    fah-sessions (tb sync) and <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent/fah-sessions
    (older artifact shape) — and warns loudly when a run with results has
    no session logs at all, so a layout drift can't silently zero the
    cost columns. Best-effort overall: old artifacts just yield no facts.
    """
    facts = {}
    try:
        candidates = list(runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent-logs/fah-sessions")) + list(
            runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent/fah-sessions")
        )
    except OSError:
        candidates = []
    if not candidates:
        # Only reachable when at least one results.json exists, so this is
        # a real run whose session logs went missing or drifted layout.
        print(
            f"[summary] warning: no fa session logs found "
            f"(*/*/*/agent*/fah-sessions under {runs_dir}) — per-trial model "
            f"unknown, cost renders n/a unless --model/env provides one",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    for sessions in candidates:
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(sessions)
        models = sorted(m for m in usage.models if m)
        facts[sessions.parent.parent.name] = {

      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider

          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="zai glm ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi needs its capability fields declared —
              # the env preconfig carries them into the booted model

              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":2000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash' or 'kimi-for-coding'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then

          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"

            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"

#!/bin/sh
# Terminal-Bench install script for the fa coding agent.
# Runs inside the task container as the tmux user (root).
set -e

mkdir -p /opt/fa
tar -xzf /installed-agent/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/fa
chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah
ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa

# Pre-seed a system-level git identity so git-touching tasks don't burn
# agent turns on `Author identity unknown` (gh-1210). System scope keeps
# repo-local config winning, so tasks whose subject is broken git config
# keep their premise. The trailing || true turns every failure path of the
# list — git-less image, failed write — into a no-op: set -e exempts the
# non-final commands of an && list but NOT the final one, so the bare list
# would still abort the install on a failed user.email write.
command -v git >/dev/null &&
    git config --system user.name fa-bench &&
    git config --system user.email fa@bench.local || true

# No user is present during benchmark runs; autopilot skips the
# critical-pattern bash interceptor that headless mode would deny.
mkdir -p ~/.fah
grep -q approvalMode ~/.fah/config.yaml 2>/dev/null ||
    printf 'approvalMode: autopilot\n' > ~/.fah/config.yaml

fa --version

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Accuracy summary for terminal-bench run dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]

Reads every <runs-dir>/*/results.json (sharded runs pin --run-id, so one
subdir per shard) and prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown accuracy table,
also appending it to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

Token/cost columns (issue #1123): total_input/output_tokens come from the
trial's fa session records (folded in by fa_agent.py at perform_task time).
Per-trial cost is derived from the pinned price table bench/pricing.json
($/Mtok, data not code); the model id is taken from the trial's synced
session records when present, else --model (or the MODEL /
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env), else the cost renders n/a — never a made-up
price. Tokens estimated where a provider omitted usage (chars/4, done by
fa_agent.py) are flagged in a note when > 0.

Issue #1339: rows whose recorded totals were lost (tb's flat-cap timeout
fabrication discards the adapter's fold — gh-1209) re-fold their usage
from the synced session logs; an agent_timeout trial that did real work
after a zero-byte takeover classifies as `recovered`, distinct from
provider hang and cap exhaustion; a test_timeout trial reads as a
terminal `no (test_timeout)` in the resolved column, while other
unresolved modes render honest `pending (mode)`; and the
unpriced line names the model ids it could not price (or says the id is
unknown).

tb exits 0 even with unresolved tasks, so the exit code is the verdict on
run COMPLETENESS only. Issue #1392 AC6: a lost/cancelled shard degrades
to an explicit `coverage: X/N` note (green-with-note) — the red verdict
is reserved for real defects: nothing produced at all, or the AC8
score-honesty contradiction (an `agent_timeout` trial whose session
shows steady sub-threshold inter-record gaps, i.e. the round-2 "killed
mid-work" class the progress-aware ladder was built to retire).
--no-fail turns the verdict off (informational per-shard tallies).

Issue #1392 AC2: the report also carries request-latency p50/p95 per
concurrency level (from each trial's bench_metrics.json) and tags the
run's concurrency level (BENCH_CONCURRENCY env, set by bench.yml's
max-concurrent input).
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import bench_metrics
import fa_usage

_PRICING_PATH = Path(_BENCH_DIR) / "pricing.json"


class Row(NamedTuple):
    """One summary row.

    rec_in/rec_out: totals as recorded in results.json (0/None when tb's
    flat-cap fabrication discarded the adapter's fold). tin/tout:
    effective totals — recorded, else re-folded from the synced session
    logs (issue #1339 AC1). checklist: the gh-1412 task-ledger coverage
    cell ("checklist: V/T [ (N unmet)]" from the trial's last hidden
    `task_ledger` record, "checklist: none" when the session carries no
    ledger).
    """

    task: str
    trial: str
    mark: str
    mode: str
    rec_in: object
    rec_out: object
    tin: object
    tout: object
    cost: object
    checklist: str = "checklist: none"


def _parse_args(argv):
    """Parse [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID].

    Single parse point (the reviewer's thread 6): --model without a
    non-empty value is a loud usage error, never a silent env fallback;
    a non-numeric expected-count is the same. Falls back to the MODEL /
    FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env only when no --model was given.
    """
    no_fail = False
    model = None
    positional = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--no-fail":
            no_fail = True
        elif arg == "--model":
            if i + 1 >= len(argv) or not argv[i + 1]:
                print(
                    "[summary] error: --model requires a model id", file=sys.stderr
                )
                sys.exit(2)
            model = argv[i + 1]
            i += 1
        else:
            positional.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if not positional:
        print(
            "[summary] error: usage: summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir>"
            " [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    try:
        expected = int(positional[1]) if len(positional) > 1 else None
    except ValueError:
        print(
            f"[summary] error: expected-count must be an integer, got:"
            f" {positional[1]!r}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    if model is None:
        model = os.environ.get("MODEL")
    if model is None:
        config = os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG")
        if config:
            try:
                model = json.loads(config).get("model")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                print(
                    "[summary] warning: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is not JSON — "
                    "ignoring it for the model id",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
    return no_fail, Path(positional[0]), expected, model


def _session_facts(runs_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """trial_name → {"model": str|None, "estimated": int,
    "input_tokens": int, "output_tokens": int} from synced sessions.

    tb ships each trial's fa sessions in the run artifacts. The glob is
    pinned to the two shipped layouts — <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent-logs/
    fah-sessions (tb sync) and <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent/fah-sessions
    (older artifact shape) — and warns loudly when a run with results has
    no session logs at all, so a layout drift can't silently zero the
    cost columns. Best-effort overall: old artifacts just yield no facts.
    """
    facts = {}
    try:
        candidates = list(runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent-logs/fah-sessions")) + list(
            runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent/fah-sessions")
        )
    except OSError:
        candidates = []
    if not candidates:
        # Only reachable when at least one results.json exists, so this is
        # a real run whose session logs went missing or drifted layout.
        print(
            f"[summary] warning: no fa session logs found "
            f"(*/*/*/agent*/fah-sessions under {runs_dir}) — per-trial model "
            f"unknown, cost renders n/a unless --model/env provides one",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    for sessions in candidates:
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(sessions)
        models = sorted(m for m in usage.models if m)
        facts[sessions.parent.parent.name] = {
            # One model per trial is the norm; mixed → None (cost n/a).
            "model": models[0] if len(models) == 1 else None,
            "estimated": usage.estimated_tokens,
            # Issue #1339: the fold fa_agent.py writes into results.json
            # can be discarded by tb's flat-cap timeout fabrication, so
            # keep the session-side totals for the summary's re-fold.
            "input_tokens": usage.input_tokens + usage.estimated_input_tokens,
            "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens + usage.estimated_output_tokens,
        }
    return facts

      - name: Resolve provider

          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
        run: |

              model="$BENCH_MODEL"

              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="zai glm ($model)"

              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH

#!/bin/sh
# Terminal-Bench install script for the fa coding agent.
# Runs inside the task container as the tmux user (root).
set -e

mkdir -p /opt/fa
tar -xzf /installed-agent/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/fa
chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah
ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa

# Pre-seed a system-level git identity so git-touching tasks don't burn
# agent turns on `Author identity unknown` (gh-1210). System scope keeps
# repo-local config winning, so tasks whose subject is broken git config
# keep their premise. The trailing || true turns every failure path of the
# list — git-less image, failed write — into a no-op: set -e exempts the
# non-final commands of an && list but NOT the final one, so the bare list
# would still abort the install on a failed user.email write.
command -v git >/dev/null &&
    git config --system user.name fa-bench &&
    git config --system user.email fa@bench.local || true

# No user is present during benchmark runs; autopilot skips the
# critical-pattern bash interceptor that headless mode would deny.
mkdir -p ~/.fah
grep -q approvalMode ~/.fah/config.yaml 2>/dev/null ||
    printf 'approvalMode: autopilot\n' > ~/.fah/config.yaml

fa --version

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Accuracy summary for terminal-bench run dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]

Reads every <runs-dir>/*/results.json (sharded runs pin --run-id, so one
subdir per shard) and prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown accuracy table,
also appending it to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

Token/cost columns (issue #1123): total_input/output_tokens come from the
trial's fa session records (folded in by fa_agent.py at perform_task time).
Per-trial cost is derived from the pinned price table bench/pricing.json
($/Mtok, data not code); the model id is taken from the trial's synced
session records when present, else --model (or the MODEL /
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env), else the cost renders n/a — never a made-up
price. Tokens estimated where a provider omitted usage (chars/4, done by
fa_agent.py) are flagged in a note when > 0.

Issue #1339: rows whose recorded totals were lost (tb's flat-cap timeout
fabrication discards the adapter's fold — gh-1209) re-fold their usage
from the synced session logs; an agent_timeout trial that did real work
after a zero-byte takeover classifies as `recovered`, distinct from
provider hang and cap exhaustion; a test_timeout trial reads as a
terminal `no (test_timeout)` in the resolved column, while other
unresolved modes render honest `pending (mode)`; and the
unpriced line names the model ids it could not price (or says the id is
unknown).

tb exits 0 even with unresolved tasks, so the exit code is the verdict on
run COMPLETENESS only. Issue #1392 AC6: a lost/cancelled shard degrades
to an explicit `coverage: X/N` note (green-with-note) — the red verdict
is reserved for real defects: nothing produced at all, or the AC8
score-honesty contradiction (an `agent_timeout` trial whose session
shows steady sub-threshold inter-record gaps, i.e. the round-2 "killed
mid-work" class the progress-aware ladder was built to retire).
--no-fail turns the verdict off (informational per-shard tallies).

Issue #1392 AC2: the report also carries request-latency p50/p95 per
concurrency level (from each trial's bench_metrics.json) and tags the
run's concurrency level (BENCH_CONCURRENCY env, set by bench.yml's
max-concurrent input).
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import bench_metrics
import fa_usage

_PRICING_PATH = Path(_BENCH_DIR) / "pricing.json"


class Row(NamedTuple):
    """One summary row.

    rec_in/rec_out: totals as recorded in results.json (0/None when tb's
    flat-cap fabrication discarded the adapter's fold). tin/tout:
    effective totals — recorded, else re-folded from the synced session
    logs (issue #1339 AC1). checklist: the gh-1412 task-ledger coverage
    cell ("checklist: V/T [ (N unmet)]" from the trial's last hidden
    `task_ledger` record, "checklist: none" when the session carries no
    ledger).
    """

    task: str
    trial: str
    mark: str
    mode: str
    rec_in: object
    rec_out: object
    tin: object
    tout: object
    cost: object
    checklist: str = "checklist: none"


def _parse_args(argv):
    """Parse [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID].

    Single parse point (the reviewer's thread 6): --model without a
    non-empty value is a loud usage error, never a silent env fallback;
    a non-numeric expected-count is the same. Falls back to the MODEL /
    FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env only when no --model was given.
    """
    no_fail = False
    model = None
    positional = []
    i = 0

    """trial_name → {"model": str|None, "estimated": int,
    "input_tokens": int, "output_tokens": int} from synced sessions.

    tb ships each trial's fa sessions in the run artifacts. The glob is
    pinned to the two shipped layouts — <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent-logs/
    fah-sessions (tb sync) and <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent/fah-sessions
    (older artifact shape) — and warns loudly when a run with results has
    no session logs at all, so a layout drift can't silently zero the
    cost columns. Best-effort overall: old artifacts just yield no facts.
    """
    facts = {}
    try:
        candidates = list(runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent-logs/fah-sessions")) + list(
            runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent/fah-sessions")
        )
    except OSError:

            f"[summary] warning: no fa session logs found "
            f"(*/*/*/agent*/fah-sessions under {runs_dir}) — per-trial model "
            f"unknown, cost renders n/a unless --model/env provides one",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    for sessions in candidates:
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(sessions)
        models = sorted(m for m in usage.models if m)
        facts[sessions.parent.parent.name] = {
            # One model per trial is the norm; mixed → None (cost n/a).
            "model": models[0] if len(models) == 1 else None,
            "estimated": usage.estimated_tokens,
            # Issue #1339: the fold fa_agent.py writes into results.json
            # can be discarded by tb's flat-cap timeout fabrication, so
            # keep the session-side totals for the summary's re-fold.
            "input_tokens": usage.input_tokens + usage.estimated_input_tokens,
            "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens + usage.estimated_output_tokens,
        }
    return facts

#!/bin/sh
# Terminal-Bench install script for the fa coding agent.
# Runs inside the task container as the tmux user (root).
set -e

mkdir -p /opt/fa
tar -xzf /installed-agent/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/fa
chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah
ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa

# Pre-seed a system-level git identity so git-touching tasks don't burn
# agent turns on `Author identity unknown` (gh-1210). System scope keeps
# repo-local config winning, so tasks whose subject is broken git config
# keep their premise. The trailing || true turns every failure path of the
# list — git-less image, failed write — into a no-op: set -e exempts the
# non-final commands of an && list but NOT the final one, so the bare list
# would still abort the install on a failed user.email write.
command -v git >/dev/null &&
    git config --system user.name fa-bench &&
    git config --system user.email fa@bench.local || true

# No user is present during benchmark runs; autopilot skips the
# critical-pattern bash interceptor that headless mode would deny.
mkdir -p ~/.fah
grep -q approvalMode ~/.fah/config.yaml 2>/dev/null ||
    printf 'approvalMode: autopilot\n' > ~/.fah/config.yaml

fa --version

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Accuracy summary for terminal-bench run dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]

Reads every <runs-dir>/*/results.json (sharded runs pin --run-id, so one
subdir per shard) and prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown accuracy table,
also appending it to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

Token/cost columns (issue #1123): total_input/output_tokens come from the
trial's fa session records (folded in by fa_agent.py at perform_task time).
Per-trial cost is derived from the pinned price table bench/pricing.json
($/Mtok, data not code); the model id is taken from the trial's synced
session records when present, else --model (or the MODEL /
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env), else the cost renders n/a — never a made-up
price. Tokens estimated where a provider omitted usage (chars/4, done by
fa_agent.py) are flagged in a note when > 0.

Issue #1339: rows whose recorded totals were lost (tb's flat-cap timeout
fabrication discards the adapter's fold — gh-1209) re-fold their usage
from the synced session logs; an agent_timeout trial that did real work
after a zero-byte takeover classifies as `recovered`, distinct from
provider hang and cap exhaustion; a test_timeout trial reads as a
terminal `no (test_timeout)` in the resolved column, while other
unresolved modes render honest `pending (mode)`; and the
unpriced line names the model ids it could not price (or says the id is
unknown).

tb exits 0 even with unresolved tasks, so the exit code is the verdict on
run COMPLETENESS only. Issue #1392 AC6: a lost/cancelled shard degrades
to an explicit `coverage: X/N` note (green-with-note) — the red verdict
is reserved for real defects: nothing produced at all, or the AC8
score-honesty contradiction (an `agent_timeout` trial whose session
shows steady sub-threshold inter-record gaps, i.e. the round-2 "killed
mid-work" class the progress-aware ladder was built to retire).
--no-fail turns the verdict off (informational per-shard tallies).

Issue #1392 AC2: the report also carries request-latency p50/p95 per
concurrency level (from each trial's bench_metrics.json) and tags the
run's concurrency level (BENCH_CONCURRENCY env, set by bench.yml's
max-concurrent input).
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import bench_metrics
import fa_usage

_PRICING_PATH = Path(_BENCH_DIR) / "pricing.json"


class Row(NamedTuple):
    """One summary row.

    rec_in/rec_out: totals as recorded in results.json (0/None when tb's
    flat-cap fabrication discarded the adapter's fold). tin/tout:
    effective totals — recorded, else re-folded from the synced session
    logs (issue #1339 AC1). checklist: the gh-1412 task-ledger coverage
    cell ("checklist: V/T [ (N unmet)]" from the trial's last hidden
    `task_ledger` record, "checklist: none" when the session carries no
    ledger).
    """

    task: str
    trial: str
    mark: str
    mode: str
    rec_in: object
    rec_out: object
    tin: object
    tout: object
    cost: object
    checklist: str = "checklist: none"


def _parse_args(argv):
    """Parse [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID].

    Single parse point (the reviewer's thread 6): --model without a
    non-empty value is a loud usage error, never a silent env fallback;
    a non-numeric expected-count is the same. Falls back to the MODEL /
    FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env only when no --model was given.
    """
    no_fail = False
    model = None
    positional = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--no-fail":
            no_fail = True
        elif arg == "--model":
            if i + 1 >= len(argv) or not argv[i + 1]:
                print(
                    "[summary] error: --model requires a model id", file=sys.stderr
                )
                sys.exit(2)
            model = argv[i + 1]
            i += 1
        else:
            positional.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if not positional:
        print(
            "[summary] error: usage: summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir>"
            " [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    try:
        expected = int(positional[1]) if len(positional) > 1 else None
    except ValueError:
        print(
            f"[summary] error: expected-count must be an integer, got:"
            f" {positional[1]!r}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    if model is None:
        model = os.environ.get("MODEL")
    if model is None:
        config = os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG")
        if config:
            try:
                model = json.loads(config).get("model")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                print(
                    "[summary] warning: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is not JSON — "
                    "ignoring it for the model id",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
    return no_fail, Path(positional[0]), expected, model


def _session_facts(runs_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """trial_name → {"model": str|None, "estimated": int,
    "input_tokens": int, "output_tokens": int} from synced sessions.

    tb ships each trial's fa sessions in the run artifacts. The glob is
    pinned to the two shipped layouts — <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent-logs/
    fah-sessions (tb sync) and <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent/fah-sessions
    (older artifact shape) — and warns loudly when a run with results has
    no session logs at all, so a layout drift can't silently zero the
    cost columns. Best-effort overall: old artifacts just yield no facts.
    """
    facts = {}
    try:
        candidates = list(runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent-logs/fah-sessions")) + list(
            runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent/fah-sessions")
        )
    except OSError:
        candidates = []
    if not candidates:
        # Only reachable when at least one results.json exists, so this is
        # a real run whose session logs went missing or drifted layout.
        print(
            f"[summary] warning: no fa session logs found "
            f"(*/*/*/agent*/fah-sessions under {runs_dir}) — per-trial model "
            f"unknown, cost renders n/a unless --model/env provides one",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    for sessions in candidates:
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(sessions)
        models = sorted(m for m in usage.models if m)
        facts[sessions.parent.parent.name] = {
            # One model per trial is the norm; mixed → None (cost n/a).
            "model": models[0] if len(models) == 1 else None,
            "estimated": usage.estimated_tokens,
            # Issue #1339: the fold fa_agent.py writes into results.json
            # can be discarded by tb's flat-cap timeout fabrication, so
            # keep the session-side totals for the summary's re-fold.
            "input_tokens": usage.input_tokens + usage.estimated_input_tokens,
            "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens + usage.estimated_output_tokens,
        }
    return facts


def _latency_facts(runs_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """concurrency level -> [first_byte_sec, ...] (raw per-request samples).

    Reads every trial's bench_metrics.json, consuming the keys
    bench_metrics.summarize_trial actually writes (`first_byte_sec` — the
    same writer the adapter calls from _write_trial_metrics; AC2).
    Percentiles are computed with bench_metrics.percentile, so the report
    and the per-trial `latency.first_byte` block share one semantics.
    Trials without the file (older artifacts) contribute nothing; corrupt
    files degrade to a warning, never a crash.
    """
    levels = {}
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(str(runs_dir / "*" / "*" / "*" / "bench_metrics.json"))):
        try:
            data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text())
        except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
            print(
                f"[summary] warning: unreadable {path}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr
            )

That keeps existing tests green (they don't set the env) and satisfies "summary header names provider/model".

#!/bin/sh
# Terminal-Bench install script for the fa coding agent.
# Runs inside the task container as the tmux user (root).
set -e

mkdir -p /opt/fa
tar -xzf /installed-agent/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/fa
chmod +x /opt/fa/bin/fah
ln -sf /opt/fa/bin/fah /usr/local/bin/fa

# Pre-seed a system-level git identity so git-touching tasks don't burn
# agent turns on `Author identity unknown` (gh-1210). System scope keeps
# repo-local config winning, so tasks whose subject is broken git config
# keep their premise. The trailing || true turns every failure path of the
# list — git-less image, failed write — into a no-op: set -e exempts the
# non-final commands of an && list but NOT the final one, so the bare list
# would still abort the install on a failed user.email write.
command -v git >/dev/null &&
    git config --system user.name fa-bench &&
    git config --system user.email fa@bench.local || true

# No user is present during benchmark runs; autopilot skips the
# critical-pattern bash interceptor that headless mode would deny.
mkdir -p ~/.fah
grep -q approvalMode ~/.fah/config.yaml 2>/dev/null ||
    printf 'approvalMode: autopilot\n' > ~/.fah/config.yaml

fa --version

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Accuracy summary for terminal-bench run dirs.

Usage:
    summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]

Reads every <runs-dir>/*/results.json (sharded runs pin --run-id, so one
subdir per shard) and prints a GitHub-flavoured-markdown accuracy table,
also appending it to $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY when set.

Token/cost columns (issue #1123): total_input/output_tokens come from the
trial's fa session records (folded in by fa_agent.py at perform_task time).
Per-trial cost is derived from the pinned price table bench/pricing.json
($/Mtok, data not code); the model id is taken from the trial's synced
session records when present, else --model (or the MODEL /
FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env), else the cost renders n/a — never a made-up
price. Tokens estimated where a provider omitted usage (chars/4, done by
fa_agent.py) are flagged in a note when > 0.

Issue #1339: rows whose recorded totals were lost (tb's flat-cap timeout
fabrication discards the adapter's fold — gh-1209) re-fold their usage
from the synced session logs; an agent_timeout trial that did real work
after a zero-byte takeover classifies as `recovered`, distinct from
provider hang and cap exhaustion; a test_timeout trial reads as a
terminal `no (test_timeout)` in the resolved column, while other
unresolved modes render honest `pending (mode)`; and the
unpriced line names the model ids it could not price (or says the id is
unknown).

tb exits 0 even with unresolved tasks, so the exit code is the verdict on
run COMPLETENESS only. Issue #1392 AC6: a lost/cancelled shard degrades
to an explicit `coverage: X/N` note (green-with-note) — the red verdict
is reserved for real defects: nothing produced at all, or the AC8
score-honesty contradiction (an `agent_timeout` trial whose session
shows steady sub-threshold inter-record gaps, i.e. the round-2 "killed
mid-work" class the progress-aware ladder was built to retire).
--no-fail turns the verdict off (informational per-shard tallies).

Issue #1392 AC2: the report also carries request-latency p50/p95 per
concurrency level (from each trial's bench_metrics.json) and tags the
run's concurrency level (BENCH_CONCURRENCY env, set by bench.yml's
max-concurrent input).
"""
import glob
import json
import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

_BENCH_DIR = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent)
if _BENCH_DIR not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, _BENCH_DIR)
import bench_metrics
import fa_usage

_PRICING_PATH = Path(_BENCH_DIR) / "pricing.json"


class Row(NamedTuple):
    """One summary row.

    rec_in/rec_out: totals as recorded in results.json (0/None when tb's
    flat-cap fabrication discarded the adapter's fold). tin/tout:
    effective totals — recorded, else re-folded from the synced session
    logs (issue #1339 AC1). checklist: the gh-1412 task-ledger coverage
    cell ("checklist: V/T [ (N unmet)]" from the trial's last hidden
    `task_ledger` record, "checklist: none" when the session carries no
    ledger).
    """

    task: str
    trial: str
    mark: str
    mode: str
    rec_in: object
    rec_out: object
    tin: object
    tout: object
    cost: object
    checklist: str = "checklist: none"


def _parse_args(argv):
    """Parse [--no-fail] <runs-dir> [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID].

    Single parse point (the reviewer's thread 6): --model without a
    non-empty value is a loud usage error, never a silent env fallback;
    a non-numeric expected-count is the same. Falls back to the MODEL /
    FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG env only when no --model was given.
    """
    no_fail = False
    model = None
    positional = []
    i = 0
    while i < len(argv):
        arg = argv[i]
        if arg == "--no-fail":
            no_fail = True
        elif arg == "--model":
            if i + 1 >= len(argv) or not argv[i + 1]:
                print(
                    "[summary] error: --model requires a model id", file=sys.stderr
                )
                sys.exit(2)
            model = argv[i + 1]
            i += 1
        else:
            positional.append(arg)
        i += 1
    if not positional:
        print(
            "[summary] error: usage: summary.py [--no-fail] <runs-dir>"
            " [expected-count] [--model MODEL_ID]",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    try:
        expected = int(positional[1]) if len(positional) > 1 else None
    except ValueError:
        print(
            f"[summary] error: expected-count must be an integer, got:"
            f" {positional[1]!r}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(2)
    if model is None:
        model = os.environ.get("MODEL")
    if model is None:
        config = os.environ.get("FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG")
        if config:
            try:
                model = json.loads(config).get("model")
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                print(
                    "[summary] warning: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is not JSON — "
                    "ignoring it for the model id",
                    file=sys.stderr,
                )
    return no_fail, Path(positional[0]), expected, model


def _session_facts(runs_dir: Path) -> dict:
    """trial_name → {"model": str|None, "estimated": int,
    "input_tokens": int, "output_tokens": int} from synced sessions.

    tb ships each trial's fa sessions in the run artifacts. The glob is
    pinned to the two shipped layouts — <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent-logs/
    fah-sessions (tb sync) and <run>/<task>/<trial>/agent/fah-sessions
    (older artifact shape) — and warns loudly when a run with results has
    no session logs at all, so a layout drift can't silently zero the
    cost columns. Best-effort overall: old artifacts just yield no facts.
    """
    facts = {}
    try:
        candidates = list(runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent-logs/fah-sessions")) + list(
            runs_dir.glob("*/*/*/agent/fah-sessions")
        )
    except OSError:
        candidates = []
    if not candidates:
        # Only reachable when at least one results.json exists, so this is
        # a real run whose session logs went missing or drifted layout.
        print(
            f"[summary] warning: no fa session logs found "
            f"(*/*/*/agent*/fah-sessions under {runs_dir}) — per-trial model "
            f"unknown, cost renders n/a unless --model/env provides one",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
    for sessions in candidates:
        usage = fa_usage.extract_from_dir(sessions)
        models = sorted(m for m in usage.models if m)
        facts[sessions.parent.parent.name] = {
            # One model per trial is the norm; mixed → None (cost n/a).
            "model": models[0] if len(models) == 1 else None,
            "estimated": usage.estimated_tokens,
            # Issue #1339: the fold fa_agent.py writes into results.json
            # can be discarded by tb's flat-cap timeout fabrication, so
            # keep the session-side totals for the summary's re-fold.
            "input_tokens": usage.input_tokens + usage.estimated_input_tokens,
            "output_tokens": usage.output_tokens + usage.estimated_output_tokens,
        }
    return facts

```yaml
      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must burn one setup minute, not 8 shards x hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the key value is never echoed (the
      # ::add-mask line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py
      # uses). Unknown provider values fail hard — never a silent
      # fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="zai glm ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi needs its capability fields declared —
              # the env preconfig carries them into the booted model
              # (catalog spec defaults would match today, an explicit
              # declaration cannot silently truncate on a catalog drift).
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":2000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash' or 'kimi-for-coding'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key base64-encoded; GitHub auto-masks
          # only the raw value, so mask the base64 form too.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

+      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
+      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
+      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
+      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
+      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
+      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
+      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
+      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
+      - name: Resolve provider
+        id: provider
+        env:
+          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
+          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
+          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
+          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          case "$PROVIDER" in
+            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)

+              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
+              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
+              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
+              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY

+              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
+              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
+                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
+              run_label="zai glm ($model)"
+              ;;
+            kimi-for-coding)
+              provider_type=kimi
+              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
+              model='k3-256k'
+              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
+              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
+              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY

+              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
+              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
+              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \

+              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
+              ;;
+            *)
+              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash' or 'kimi-for-coding'"; exit 1 ;;

+          fi

+          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
+          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"

+            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
+            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
+            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
+            echo "bench_model=$model"
+            echo "run_label=$run_label"
+          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

tar -xzf /installed-agent/fa-bundle.tar.gz -C /opt/fa

# Pre-seed a system-level git identity so git-touching tasks don't burn
# agent turns on `Author identity unknown` (gh-1210). System scope keeps
# repo-local config winning, so tasks whose subject is broken git config
# keep their premise. The trailing || true turns every failure path of the
# list — git-less image, failed write — into a no-op: set -e exempts the
# non-final commands of an && list but NOT the final one, so the bare list
# would still abort the install on a failed user.email write.
command -v git >/dev/null &&
    git config --system user.name fa-bench &&
    git config --system user.email fa@bench.local || true

# critical-pattern bash interceptor that headless mode would deny.
mkdir -p ~/.fah
